what: Latent path-resolution bug in preRead/preEdit hooks (src/memory/hooks/handlers.ts:125-188 and :195-245): `const filePath = input.tool_input?.file_path` is used raw in hasRecalledFile(projectRoot, sessionId, filePath) without resolving relative→absolute first. But trackRecall (line 611) DOES resolve: `const absPath = path.isAbsolute(p) ? p : path.join(projectRoot, p)` before writing `file|<abs>` to tracking. Asymmetry: if filePath comes in relative, the `file|` tracking line stored is absolute but the lookup compares against the relative string → no match → encountered=false forever → every read is treated as first-read → hard block. Production-safe today because Claude Code's Read/Edit tools require absolute paths in the tool schema. But any caller that passes relative (tests, future MCP-to-MCP integrations, custom hooks) hits the soft-block transition break. One-line fix at line 126 and 196: `const filePath = rawFilePath && !path.isAbsolute(rawFilePath) ? path.resolve(projectRoot, rawFilePath) : rawFilePath`. Same fix for preEdit. Low risk, high robustness. Was not caught by existing tests because hooks.test.ts uses absolute paths throughout.
why: Discovered during 2026-04-22 full-scenario simulation when relative-path input to pre-read unexpectedly blocked instead of going soft despite file| tracking being populated. Documented so a future robustness pass doesn't have to re-derive the root cause.
